questions.q: What does the Bronze layer's PySpark code deliberately NOT do to the raw sales extract?
options: Read the file using spark.read
Deduplicate, type-cast, or filter out any rows
Use an option to read a header row
Write the result as a Delta table
questions.explain: Bronze lands the data exactly as the source sent it — cleaning, deduplication, and casting are explicitly Silver's job in the next lesson.

questions.q: Why does the Bronze write use mode("append") instead of mode("overwrite")?
options: Because Delta Lake does not support the overwrite mode
Because append mode runs faster on small files
So each day's extract adds to the full history instead of erasing the previous day's raw records
Because overwrite mode would delete the entire database
questions.explain: Bronze is meant to be the layer you can always go back to — append mode preserves every previous day's landed data instead of replacing it.

questions.q: Why is it acceptable to use inferSchema in the Bronze read, when it won't be used later in the pipeline?
options: Because nothing downstream depends on the guessed types being perfect yet — that precision matters starting in Silver
Because JSON files cannot have their schema inferred
Because Gold tables cannot use explicitly declared schemas
Because inferSchema is required for any CSV file to be readable at all
questions.explain: Bronze just needs to land the file; explicit, intentional type casting starts in Lesson 4 once the numbers actually need to be correct.

questions.q: The in-store POS extract and the online storefront's order events are read with two different methods. Which pair is correct?
options: Both must be converted to XML before spark.read can load them
spark.read.csv(...) for the POS extract, spark.read.json(...) for the online orders
Both are read with spark.read.parquet(...)
spark.read.json(...) for the POS extract, spark.read.csv(...) for the online orders
questions.explain: The in-store POS system produces a CSV extract; the online storefront produces JSON order events — each gets the matching PySpark reader.

questions.q: Why is it fine that the in-store and online data have different raw column names and shapes when they both land in bronze.daily_sales_raw?
options: Because PySpark refuses to write two different schemas to the same table
Because reconciling the two shapes into one common structure is explicitly Silver's job, not Bronze's
Because the online data gets discarded before reaching Bronze
Because Delta tables automatically rename mismatched columns on write
questions.explain: Bronze's job is only to preserve what arrived; schema unification across sources happens in the Bronze-to-Silver transformation in Lesson 4.
